held.title: Typed `WorkspaceError::MissingPyprojectToml` is replaced by a plain string error, so callers can no longer detect it.
held.body: Before this change the `WorkspaceError` reached callers through `?`, so `anyhow::Error::downcast_ref::<WorkspaceError>()` could find it. Now `anyhow!("{}\n\nhint: ...", err)` creates a new string error. Any caller that branches on `MissingPyprojectToml` will stop matching it, for example a fallback or strictness check in the `uv version` dispatch. I could not see the callers of `project_version`/`find_target`, so I can't confirm that any of them downcast. To keep the error type, wrap it instead, e.g. `anyhow::Error::from(err).context(...)`, or put the hint in a typed error or in the dispatch layer. The same `map_err` block also appears twice and could be moved into one helper.
